New opening hours for the library during exam weeks
A plan to add more group study rooms to the library
Rules about the noise level allowed in the group study rooms

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): rooms are now reserved in the app instead of on paper sheets. B, C and D bring in topics the notice never mentions (hours, new rooms, noise).

screens.title: Email: tuition payment plan
text:
From: Student Accounts Office
To: Daniel Okafor
Subject: Your payment plan request

Dear Daniel, thank you for applying to pay this semester's tuition in installments. Your plan has been approved: the balance will be divided into four equal payments, due on the first day of each month from September to December. There is a one-time setup fee of $25, which will be added to your first payment. Please note that a payment more than ten days late will cancel the plan, and the full remaining balance will then be due at once.
— Student Accounts Office

questions.stem: Why did the office write to Daniel?
options: To confirm that his request to pay in parts was accepted
To remind him that his first payment is already overdue
To explain why his application for a payment plan was refused
To ask him to choose how many payments he would like to make

why.en: Purpose (paraphrase): "Your plan has been approved." B is not stated: no payment is late yet. C reverses the decision; D is wrong because the office has already set four payments.
why.tr: Amaç (parafraz): "Your plan has been approved." B metinde yok, henüz geciken bir ödeme yok. C kararı tersine çeviriyor; D yanlış, çünkü ofis dört taksiti zaten belirlemiş.
why.es: Propósito (paráfrasis): "Your plan has been approved." B no se dice: todavía no hay ningún pago atrasado. C invierte la decisión; D es incorrecta porque la oficina ya fijó cuatro pagos.

questions.stem: What is true about the $25 fee?
options: It is charged every month together with each payment
It will be paid as part of the September payment
It is charged only if a payment arrives late
It can be avoided by paying the full balance in December

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): the fee is "one-time" and "added to your first payment", which is due in September. A contradicts "one-time"; C confuses the fee with the late-payment rule.
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): ücret "tek seferlik" ve "ilk ödemeye ekleniyor"; ilk ödeme Eylül'de. A "one-time" ifadesiyle çelişiyor; C ücreti gecikme kuralıyla karıştırıyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): la tarifa es "one-time" y se "añade al primer pago", que vence en septiembre. A contradice "one-time"; C confunde la tarifa con la regla de los pagos atrasados.

questions.stem: What would happen if Daniel paid his October installment on October 15?
options: He would be charged a second setup fee of $25
His November payment would be moved to a later date
He would have to pay everything he still owes immediately
Nothing would happen, because payments may be up to twenty days late

why.en: Inference: October 15 is fourteen days late, more than ten, so the plan is cancelled and "the full remaining balance" becomes due. D invents a twenty-day limit; A and B are never mentioned.
why.tr: Çıkarım: 15 Ekim on dört gün gecikme demek, yani on günden fazla; plan iptal olur ve "kalan borcun tamamı" ödenmeli. D yirmi günlük bir süre uyduruyor; A ve B hiç geçmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: el 15 de octubre son catorce días de retraso, más de diez, así que el plan se cancela y vence "todo el saldo pendiente". D inventa un límite de veinte días; A y B no se mencionan.

screens.title: How Printing Changed Spelling
text: Before the printing press reached England in the late fifteenth century, English spelling varied widely. Writers spelled words as they heard them, and the same scribe might write a common word in two or three ways on a single page.

Printing gradually reduced this variety. Because a printer produced hundreds of identical copies, readers across the country began to see the same forms again and again. Printers also had practical reasons to settle on fixed spellings, since consistent forms made it faster to set the metal type for each page.

The change was slow, however. Early printers sometimes added or removed letters simply to fill a line evenly, and many spellings did not become stable until dictionaries appeared in the eighteenth century. Even so, historians generally agree that printing started the movement toward standard spelling.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why scribes preferred writing by hand to using the printing press
How a machine for copying text made written words more alike
Why eighteenth-century dictionaries contained many spelling mistakes
How printers set metal type to produce identical pages quickly

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase of "printing started the movement toward standard spelling"). D is only one supporting detail; C is not stated; A invents a preference.
why.tr: Ana fikir ("printing started the movement toward standard spelling" ifadesinin parafrazı). D yalnızca destekleyici bir ayrıntı; C metinde yok; A bir tercih uyduruyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis de "printing started the movement toward standard spelling"). D es solo un detalle de apoyo; C no se dice; A inventa una preferencia.

questions.stem: The word "settle on" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: argue about
decide on
look for
write down

why.en: Vocabulary in context: printers wanted to "settle on fixed spellings", that is, choose them and keep them. A is close to the opposite; C and D do not fit "fixed spellings".
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: matbaacılar "settle on fixed spellings" istiyordu, yani yazımları seçip korumak. A neredeyse tersi; C ve D "fixed spellings" ile uyuşmuyor.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: los impresores querían "settle on fixed spellings", es decir, elegirlas y mantenerlas. A es casi lo contrario; C y D no encajan con "fixed spellings".

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that printers added or removed letters to fill a line?
options: To show that printing did not make spelling consistent right away
To explain why printed books were usually cheaper than handwritten ones
To suggest that printers did not know how to spell correctly
To prove that dictionaries were based on early printed books

why.en: Author's purpose: the example supports "The change was slow". C reads too much into it: the letters changed for layout, not from ignorance. B and D are never discussed.
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: örnek "The change was slow" ifadesini destekliyor. C fazla yorum katıyor: harfler bilgisizlikten değil sayfa düzeni için değişiyordu. B ve D hiç ele alınmıyor.
why.es: Propósito del autor: el ejemplo apoya "The change was slow". C interpreta de más: las letras cambiaban por la maquetación, no por ignorancia. B y D no se tratan.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about spelling before the printing press?
options: Most writers followed the rules of an early English dictionary
Spelling depended more on how words sounded to each writer
Only scribes in large cities were allowed to write official documents
Readers found handwritten texts easier to understand than printed ones

why.en: Inference from "Writers spelled words as they heard them". A contradicts the timeline: dictionaries came much later. C and D are not supported.
why.tr: "Writers spelled words as they heard them" ifadesinden çıkarım. A zaman sırasıyla çelişiyor: sözlükler çok sonra geldi. C ve D metinle desteklenmiyor.
why.es: Inferencia a partir de "Writers spelled words as they heard them". A contradice la cronología: los diccionarios llegaron mucho después. C y D no tienen apoyo.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, why did printers prefer consistent spellings?
options: Readers complained when words appeared in unfamiliar forms
The government required printers to use official spellings
It saved time when they were getting pages ready
Scribes refused to work with printers who changed spellings

why.en: Detail (paraphrase of "consistent forms made it faster to set the metal type"). A, B and D give reasons the passage never mentions.
why.tr: Ayrıntı ("consistent forms made it faster to set the metal type" ifadesinin parafrazı). A, B ve D metinde hiç geçmeyen gerekçeler veriyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "consistent forms made it faster to set the metal type"). A, B y D dan razones que el texto nunca menciona.

hard.title: Accessibility Office: exam accommodations
text: Accessibility Services — Requesting Exam Accommodations

Students registered with Accessibility Services who need extended time or a separate room for an exam must submit a request through the online portal at least seven days before the exam. Requests submitted later will be considered only if space and staff are available, and approval cannot be guaranteed. Instructors are notified automatically once a request is approved, so students need not deliver letters in person. Accommodations approved for midterm exams do not carry over to final exams; a new request is required for each.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To explain how and when students should ask for special exam arrangements
To announce that the Accessibility Services office is moving to a new building
To tell instructors how to prepare separate rooms for their final exams
To invite students to register with Accessibility Services before midterms

why.en: Main purpose (paraphrase): the notice sets out the procedure and the deadline for accommodation requests. C reverses the audience: instructors are only notified. D is a precondition, not the purpose.
why.tr: Ana amaç (parafraz): duyuru düzenleme taleplerinin nasıl ve ne zamana kadar yapılacağını anlatıyor. C hitap edilen kişiyi tersine çeviriyor; öğretim üyeleri yalnızca bilgilendiriliyor. D bir ön koşul, amaç değil.
why.es: Propósito principal (paráfrasis): el aviso explica el procedimiento y el plazo para pedir adaptaciones. C invierte el destinatario: a los profesores solo se les avisa. D es un requisito previo, no el propósito.

questions.stem: A student submits a request four days before an exam. What can be inferred?
options: The request will be rejected without being reviewed
The student must deliver a letter to the instructor in person
The request might be approved, but only if resources allow
The exam will be moved to give the office more time

why.en: Inference: late requests are "considered only if space and staff are available", so approval is possible but uncertain. A goes too far ("rejected without being reviewed"); B contradicts "need not deliver letters in person".
why.tr: Çıkarım: geç talepler "yer ve personel varsa" değerlendiriliyor; onay mümkün ama kesin değil. A fazla ileri gidiyor ("incelenmeden reddedilir"); B "need not deliver letters in person" ifadesiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: las solicitudes tardías se consideran "solo si hay espacio y personal", así que la aprobación es posible pero no segura. A va demasiado lejos ("rechazada sin revisarla"); B contradice "need not deliver letters in person".

questions.stem: According to the notice, what must a student who had extended time for a midterm do before the final exam?
options: Nothing, because the midterm arrangement continues automatically
Ask the instructor to sign a letter confirming the arrangement
Register again with Accessibility Services as a new student
Ask once more, because each permission lasts for one exam period

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): approvals "do not carry over to final exams; a new request is required". A is the trap: it assumes the midterm approval continues. C confuses a new request with a new registration.
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): onaylar "final sınavlarına geçmiyor; yeni bir talep gerekiyor". A tuzak: ara sınav onayının sürdüğünü varsayıyor. C yeni talebi yeni kayıtla karıştırıyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): las aprobaciones "no se trasladan a los exámenes finales; se necesita una nueva solicitud". A es la trampa: supone que la aprobación del parcial sigue. C confunde una nueva solicitud con un nuevo registro.

hard.title: Why Wages Rarely Fall
hard.directions: Read an Academic Passage — upper module
text: Elementary economic theory predicts that when the demand for labor declines, wages should fall until employers are again willing to hire everyone seeking work. Empirical studies, however, consistently find that nominal wages are remarkably resistant to reduction, even during severe recessions; firms typically respond to weaker demand by dismissing employees rather than by lowering pay.

Economists have proposed several explanations for this rigidity. Surveys of managers indicate that wage cuts are perceived as unfair and consequently damage morale, diminishing the effort of the very employees a firm most wishes to retain. Efficiency-wage theory extends this reasoning, arguing that paying above the market rate can be profitable because it reduces turnover and the considerable costs of recruiting and training replacements.

Wage rigidity has significant consequences. Because pay does not adjust, the burden of a downturn is concentrated on those who lose their jobs rather than distributed across the entire workforce, which may help explain why unemployment rises so sharply during recessions.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The reasons wages seldom fall and what this means during downturns
The methods firms use to recruit and train new employees cheaply
The ways in which economic theory predicts the length of recessions
The advantages of lowering wages instead of dismissing workers

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): the passage explains why wages are rigid and how this concentrates the cost of recessions. D reverses the evidence; B is a minor detail inside one explanation.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): metin ücretlerin neden düşmediğini ve bunun durgunluğun yükünü nasıl yoğunlaştırdığını anlatıyor. D kanıtı tersine çeviriyor; B bir açıklamanın içindeki küçük bir ayrıntı.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): el texto explica por qué los salarios son rígidos y cómo eso concentra el coste de las recesiones. D invierte la evidencia; B es un detalle menor dentro de una explicación.

questions.stem: The word "rigidity" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: unfair treatment
unwillingness to change
a period of rapid growth
great complexity

why.en: Vocabulary in context: "this rigidity" refers back to wages being "resistant to reduction", that is, not changing. A is the reason given by managers, not the meaning of the word.
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: "this rigidity" ücretlerin "resistant to reduction" olmasına, yani değişmemesine işaret ediyor. A yöneticilerin gerekçesi, kelimenin anlamı değil.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: "this rigidity" remite a que los salarios son "resistant to reduction", es decir, que no cambian. A es la razón que dan los directivos, no el significado de la palabra.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention surveys of managers?
options: To show that managers misunderstand basic economic theory
To prove that recessions are caused by unfair treatment of employees
To support the claim that cutting pay can lower workers' effort
To compare how often firms dismiss workers in different countries

why.en: Author's purpose: the surveys support the idea that wage cuts "damage morale, diminishing the effort" of employees. B overstates the claim into a cause of recessions; A and D are not in the passage.
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: anketler ücret kesintisinin "moral bozduğu ve çabayı azalttığı" fikrini destekliyor. B iddiayı durgunluğun nedenine dönüştürerek abartıyor; A ve D metinde yok.
why.es: Propósito del autor: las encuestas apoyan la idea de que los recortes "dañan la moral y reducen el esfuerzo". B exagera la idea hasta convertirla en causa de las recesiones; A y D no están en el texto.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from efficiency-wage theory?
options: Generous salaries can end up saving a company money
Firms that pay high wages rarely need to hire new employees at all
Training new employees costs less than keeping experienced ones
Employers should reduce wages whenever demand for labor declines

why.en: Inference: paying above the market rate "can be profitable" because it lowers turnover costs. B overstates "reduces turnover" as "rarely need to hire"; C reverses the costs; D contradicts the theory.
why.tr: Çıkarım: piyasanın üstünde ödemek, işten ayrılma maliyetini düşürdüğü için "kârlı olabilir". B "reduces turnover" ifadesini "neredeyse hiç işe alım gerekmez" diye abartıyor; C maliyetleri tersine çeviriyor; D teoriyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: pagar por encima del mercado "puede ser rentable" porque reduce los costes de rotación. B exagera "reduces turnover" como "casi nunca necesitan contratar"; C invierte los costes; D contradice la teoría.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, what is one effect of wage rigidity?
options: All employees share equally in the losses of a recession
The costs of a downturn fall mainly on workers who are dismissed
Firms recover more slowly because their total wage costs remain high
Unemployment remains steady even when demand for labor falls

why.en: Detail (paraphrase of "the burden of a downturn is concentrated on those who lose their jobs"). A is the opposite; D contradicts "unemployment rises so sharply"; C is never stated.
why.tr: Ayrıntı ("the burden of a downturn is concentrated on those who lose their jobs" ifadesinin parafrazı). A tam tersi; D "unemployment rises so sharply" ifadesiyle çelişiyor; C hiç söylenmiyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "the burden of a downturn is concentrated on those who lose their jobs"). A es lo contrario; D contradice "unemployment rises so sharply"; C no se dice.

easy.title: Flowers That Open at Night
easy.directions: Read an Academic Passage — lower module
text: Most flowers open during the day, when bees and butterflies are busy. Some plants, however, open their flowers only at night. These plants depend on night animals, such as moths and bats, to carry their pollen from flower to flower.

Night flowers are often white or pale, so they are easy to see in moonlight. Many also have a strong, sweet smell that moths can follow from far away. Flowers visited by bats are usually large and strong, because bats are heavy and push their heads deep inside to drink.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why bees and butterflies stop working at night
How some flowers are suited to animals that visit at night
Why moths are more useful to plants than bats are
How gardeners can grow flowers that bloom only in the moonlight

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): the passage describes how night flowers match moths and bats. A misreads the first sentence; C and D are never discussed.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): metin gece açan çiçeklerin güvelere ve yarasalara nasıl uyduğunu anlatıyor. A ilk cümleyi yanlış okuyor; C ve D hiç ele alınmıyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): el texto describe cómo las flores nocturnas se adaptan a las polillas y los murciélagos. A malinterpreta la primera frase; C y D no se tratan.

questions.stem: The word "pale" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: light in color
very small
easy to break
sweet-smelling

why.en: Vocabulary in context: "white or pale" flowers are "easy to see in moonlight", so pale means light in color. D describes the smell mentioned in the next sentence.
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: "white or pale" çiçekler "ay ışığında kolay görülüyor"; pale açık renkli demek. D bir sonraki cümledeki kokuyu anlatıyor.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: las flores "white or pale" son "fáciles de ver a la luz de la luna", así que pale significa de color claro. D describe el olor de la frase siguiente.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that bats are heavy?
options: To explain why some night flowers are large and strong
To show that bats are dangerous to small plants
To compare the size of bats with the much smaller size of moths
To explain why bats cannot see in the moonlight

why.en: Author's purpose: the bats' weight explains why the flowers they visit are "large and strong". B and D are not stated; C is not the point being made.
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: yarasaların ağırlığı, ziyaret ettikleri çiçeklerin neden "large and strong" olduğunu açıklıyor. B ve D metinde yok; C anlatılmak istenen nokta değil.
why.es: Propósito del autor: el peso de los murciélagos explica por qué las flores que visitan son "large and strong". B y D no se dicen; C no es la idea que se quiere mostrar.

screens.title: Academic Talk: How fog forms
screens.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in a meteorology class.

audio.text: Today let's talk about fog, which is really just a cloud that forms at ground level. Fog appears when the air near the ground cools until it can't hold all of its water vapor, so the extra vapor condenses into tiny droplets. One common type is radiation fog. On clear, calm nights, the ground loses heat quickly into the sky, and it cools the air just above it. By early morning, valleys can fill with fog, because cold air is heavier and collects in low places. Once the sun warms the ground, this kind of fog usually disappears by midmorning.

A second type, advection fog, forms in a different way. Here, warm, moist air moves across a cold surface, such as a cold ocean current. The air is cooled from below, and fog develops even when it's windy. That's why some coastal cities can be foggy for days in summer, when the land is hot but the water offshore stays cold. So if you want to predict fog, don't just look at the temperature. Look at the wind, the sky, and the kind of surface the air is moving over.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?
options: Why fog is more dangerous than other kinds of clouds
Two different ways in which fog develops
How the sun heats the ground in the morning
Why coastal cities have hotter summers than valleys

why.en: Main idea: the talk explains radiation fog and advection fog. C is only a detail about radiation fog; A and D are not discussed.
why.tr: Ana fikir: konuşma radyasyon sisini ve adveksiyon sisini açıklıyor. C radyasyon sisiyle ilgili yalnızca bir ayrıntı; A ve D ele alınmıyor.
why.es: Idea principal: la charla explica la niebla de radiación y la de advección. C es solo un detalle sobre la niebla de radiación; A y D no se tratan.

questions.stem: According to the professor, why do valleys fill with fog?
options: Wind pushes the fog down from the hills
Valleys receive less sunlight in the evening
Rivers in valleys release warm water vapor
Cold air sinks and gathers in low areas

why.en: Detail (paraphrase of "cold air is heavier and collects in low places"). A and C invent causes; B is not mentioned.
why.tr: Ayrıntı ("cold air is heavier and collects in low places" ifadesinin parafrazı). A ve C neden uyduruyor; B hiç geçmiyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "cold air is heavier and collects in low places"). A y C inventan causas; B no se menciona.

questions.stem: Why does the professor mention coastal cities in summer?
options: To show that advection fog can form even when the land is hot
To explain why radiation fog disappears by midmorning
To argue that fog is more common in summer than in winter
To compare the temperature of the ocean with that of nearby rivers

why.en: Function: the example shows that advection fog depends on warm air over cold water, so it appears even on hot days. B belongs to radiation fog; C overgeneralizes; D is not discussed.
why.tr: İşlev: örnek, adveksiyon sisinin soğuk suyun üstündeki sıcak havaya bağlı olduğunu, yani sıcak günlerde bile oluştuğunu gösteriyor. B radyasyon sisine ait; C aşırı genelleme; D ele alınmıyor.
why.es: Función: el ejemplo muestra que la niebla de advección depende de aire cálido sobre agua fría, así que aparece incluso en días calurosos. B corresponde a la niebla de radiación; C generaliza en exceso; D no se trata.

questions.stem: What would most likely prevent radiation fog from forming?
options: A cold ocean current near the coast
Very calm air during the night
A layer of clouds covering the night sky
A valley surrounded by high hills

why.en: Inference: radiation fog needs "clear, calm nights" so the ground can lose heat into the sky; clouds would keep that heat in. B and D would help fog form; A belongs to advection fog.
why.tr: Çıkarım: radyasyon sisi zeminin ısısını gökyüzüne verebilmesi için "açık ve sakin gecelere" ihtiyaç duyar; bulutlar bu ısıyı tutar. B ve D sisin oluşmasına yardım eder; A adveksiyon sisine ait.
why.es: Inferencia: la niebla de radiación necesita "noches despejadas y tranquilas" para que el suelo pierda calor hacia el cielo; las nubes retendrían ese calor. B y D favorecerían la niebla; A corresponde a la niebla de advección.

hard.title: Academic Talk: What ice cores record
hard.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in an earth science class.

audio.text: When snow falls on a large ice sheet, such as the one covering Antarctica, it doesn't melt. Year after year, new layers pile up, and the weight of the snow above slowly presses the older layers into solid ice. As this happens, tiny bubbles of air become trapped inside. Those bubbles are, in effect, samples of the atmosphere from the time the snow fell.

By drilling deep into the ice and pulling out long cylinders, which we call ice cores, researchers can measure what the air contained thousands of years ago. The deepest Antarctic cores reach back roughly eight hundred thousand years. Scientists can also estimate past temperatures from the chemistry of the ice itself, since snow that falls in colder periods contains a slightly different mix of oxygen atoms.

Now, the method has limits. Near the surface, the snow hasn't sealed yet, so air can still move between the layers. This means the air in a bubble is always somewhat younger than the ice around it, sometimes by thousands of years, and researchers have to correct for that gap before they compare the two records.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?
options: How layers of ice preserve information about past climates
Why the Antarctic ice sheet is now melting faster than ever before
How researchers drill through rock beneath the ice
Why snow in cold periods contains more oxygen

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): ice cores record past air and temperatures, with one limitation. B is never mentioned; D distorts the detail about "a slightly different mix" of oxygen atoms.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): buz karotları geçmişin havasını ve sıcaklıklarını kaydeder, bir sınırlamayla. B hiç geçmiyor; D oksijen atomlarının "biraz farklı karışımı" ayrıntısını çarpıtıyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): los testigos de hielo registran el aire y las temperaturas del pasado, con una limitación. B no se menciona; D deforma el detalle de "una mezcla algo distinta" de átomos de oxígeno.

Gases released by the rock under the ice
Air from roughly the period when the snow fell
Oxygen produced by the ice as it forms

why.tr: Ayrıntı ("samples of the atmosphere from the time the snow fell" ifadesinin parafrazı). A "it doesn't melt" ile çelişiyor; B ve D söylenmiyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "samples of the atmosphere from the time the snow fell"). A contradice "it doesn't melt"; B y D no se dicen.

questions.stem: Why does the professor mention oxygen atoms?
options: To explain how temperatures of the past can be estimated
To show that the air in the bubbles is younger than the ice itself
To describe how snow is pressed into solid ice
To explain why the deepest cores are so old

why.en: Function: the mix of oxygen atoms in the ice is the clue to past temperatures. B is the point of the last paragraph, not of this detail; C and D are separate details.
why.tr: İşlev: buzdaki oksijen atomlarının karışımı geçmiş sıcaklıkların ipucu. B son paragrafın konusu, bu ayrıntının değil; C ve D ayrı ayrıntılar.
why.es: Función: la mezcla de átomos de oxígeno en el hielo es la pista de las temperaturas pasadas. B es la idea del último párrafo, no de este detalle; C y D son detalles distintos.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about comparing the air record with the temperature record?
options: The two records always match exactly in age
The air in a bubble is usually older than the ice that holds it
Researchers cannot compare the two records at all

why.en: Inference: because the air is "somewhat younger than the ice", researchers "have to correct for that gap" first. B is the direction trap: the air is younger, not older. A ignores the gap; C goes too far.
why.tr: Çıkarım: hava "buzdan biraz daha genç" olduğu için araştırmacılar önce "bu farkı düzeltmek zorunda". B yön tuzağı: hava daha yaşlı değil, daha genç. A farkı görmüyor; C fazla ileri gidiyor.
why.es: Inferencia: como el aire es "algo más joven que el hielo", los investigadores "tienen que corregir esa diferencia" antes. B es la trampa de la dirección: el aire es más joven, no más viejo. A ignora la diferencia; C va demasiado lejos.

hard.title: Academic Talk: Why early photos look empty
hard.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in a history of photography class.

audio.text: Let's look at one of the earliest photographs of people, taken in Paris in 1838 by Louis Daguerre. It shows a boulevard that was normally full of traffic, yet the street appears almost empty. The reason is the exposure time. Daguerre's plates needed several minutes of light to record an image, so anything that moved, such as carriages or people walking, simply didn't stay in one place long enough to appear.

There's one exception, though, and it's easy to miss. In the lower corner, you can make out a man who seems to be having his boots polished. Because he stood still for minutes, he became, quite by accident, one of the first people ever photographed.

Long exposures shaped early portrait photography too. Sitters had to hold their position for a long time, and studios used hidden metal stands to support their heads. This is one reason people in early portraits rarely smile: holding a natural smile for that long is almost impossible. As the chemistry improved over the following decades, exposure times dropped to a few seconds, and photographers could finally capture busy streets as they really looked.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?
options: How the long time needed to record an image affected early photographs
Why Louis Daguerre preferred photographing empty streets to photographing people
How studios built metal stands for early portrait cameras
Why people in the 1800s rarely smiled in daily life

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): exposure time explains the empty street, the accidental portrait and the serious faces. C and D twist details about portraits; B is never stated.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): pozlama süresi boş sokağı, tesadüfi portreyi ve ciddi yüzleri açıklıyor. C ve D portrelerle ilgili ayrıntıları çarpıtıyor; B hiç söylenmiyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): el tiempo de exposición explica la calle vacía, el retrato accidental y las caras serias. C y D deforman detalles sobre los retratos; B no se dice.

why.tr: Ayrıntı ("anything that moved ... didn't stay in one place long enough to appear" ifadesinin parafrazı). A ve B profesörün vermediği açıklamalar; D uydurma.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "anything that moved ... didn't stay in one place long enough to appear"). A y B dan explicaciones que la profesora no da; D es inventada.

questions.stem: Why does the professor mention the man having his boots polished?

To explain why Daguerre chose that particular boulevard for his photograph
To suggest that the man knew he was being photographed

why.en: Function: he appears because "he stood still for minutes", which confirms the explanation about exposure time. D contradicts "quite by accident"; B and C are not the point.
why.tr: İşlev: adam "dakikalarca kıpırdamadan durduğu" için görünüyor; bu da pozlama süresi açıklamasını doğruluyor. D "quite by accident" ile çelişiyor; B ve C asıl amaç değil.
why.es: Función: el hombre aparece porque "se quedó quieto varios minutos", lo que confirma la explicación sobre el tiempo de exposición. D contradice "quite by accident"; B y C no son la idea.

audio.text: Beavers are famous for building dams across small rivers. They use sticks, mud and stones to block the water, and a pond forms behind the dam. screens.prompt: Your professor is teaching a class on education policy. Write a post responding to the professor's question. Express and support your opinion, and make a contribution to the discussion in your own words.

professor.name: Okonkwo
professor.post: Many universities let students take a few courses outside their major on a pass/fail basis instead of receiving a letter grade. Supporters say this encourages students to explore subjects they would otherwise avoid. Critics worry that students put in less effort when a grade does not count. Should universities allow students to take some courses pass/fail? Why or why not?

students.name: Lena
students.post: Yes, they should. I wanted to take a physics course last year, but I was afraid a low grade would hurt my scholarship, so I chose something easier instead. With a pass/fail option, students can try difficult subjects without risking their grade average, and that is what university should be about.

students.name: Marco
students.post: I'm not convinced. When I know a grade does not really matter, I study only enough to pass, and I think many students are the same. Employers and graduate schools also look closely at transcripts, so a list of passes might make it harder to see what a student actually learned.
